phaseA.primaryTacticalProblem: LW has already entered as second pivot on the left six; LB loses the drive; first pivot still occupies left half — stacked and useless
phaseA.exactDecisionFork: Sprint back to width to reopen left stretch vs stay fighting as crowded second pivot
phaseA.whyLwNative: Trains LW–LB–left-pivot congestion after an entry already happened — complementary to 948 (don't enter onto pivot), not the same lesson
phaseA.closestRw: scn_bank_918 (short return after jump when RB drew two) — different trigger and role
phaseA.whyNotSame: 918 is airborne short return after RB bind; 945 is second-pivot exit when LB drive dies and left six is stacked
phaseA.closestOther: LW 948 (don't enter) — complementary before/after entry pair

phaseA.primaryTacticalProblem: First wave died through the middle/right; defence half-set; left wing defender still late on the left lane
phaseA.exactDecisionFork: One more timed left-side advantage action (ask/arrive) vs full positional reset
phaseA.whyLwNative: Second-wave exploitation specifically because LEFT WD is late after the first wave collapsed elsewhere — not generic 'hold width in 3v2'
phaseA.closestRw: scn_bank_877 (second wave: stop forcing when advantage gone)
phaseA.whyNotSame: 877 teaches STOP when advantage is gone; 947 teaches CONTINUE one left action while WD is still late — opposite fork, left-lane cue

phaseA.primaryTacticalProblem: Opposing right back drives; you are tempted to ball-watch; opposing right wing starts back-door behind you on the left side
phaseA.exactDecisionFork: Feel/deny the back-door runner with contact vs chase the ball into the drive and lose the wing
phaseA.whyLwNative: Left-side wing defender vs opposing RB + RW geometry; teaches deny-entry, not handover/help (RW 880)
phaseA.closestRw: scn_bank_880 (protect pass until handover) — different responsibility
phaseA.whyNotSame: 880 is pass-lane protect until handover call; 949 is denying the wing runner's back-door while ball-watching temptation
phaseA.closestOther: RW defence has no deny-backdoor family
phaseA.exceptionalNote: Keeps a distinct defensive lesson in the pilot after removing handover-duplicate 949

phaseA.primaryTacticalProblem: You gave a controlled help step inside; ball reverses toward the opposing right wing; skip threat is live
phaseA.exactDecisionFork: Sprint recover to the wing before the skip arrives vs stay helping inside because the drive 'still looks dangerous'
phaseA.whyLwNative: Recovery timing after left-side help — distinct from handover (880), help-after-handover (928), and transition own-lane (929)
phaseA.closestRw: scn_bank_928 (help after handover) — requires handover already completed
phaseA.whyNotSame: 950 has NO handover; ball reverses while you are still the wing; recovery race is the lesson
phaseA.coverageGap: recovery to wing after inside help
